data.title: The Fed Is Focused on Inflation, but the Labor Market Needs Attention, Too — Barrons.com
data.description:
By Megan Leonhardt

Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh devoted just a few words to the labor market at his news conference on Oct. 28, assuring the audience that employment conditions are stable. "Job gains have kept pace with the workforce, and the unemployment rate has changed little, so on the employment side of the Fed's dual mandate, conditions are quite positive," he said, before pivoting to a discussion of inflation.

Yet the labor outlook may not be as rosy as Warsh suggested. Payroll growth is noticeably above last year's pace, but this year's average monthly gain of 68,000 isn't especially strong, and the drivers behind sluggish job growth aren't fading.

Policymakers can't afford to ignore the weakness. Higher short-term interest rates may help to cool inflation, but they could put further strain on the labor market's health.

The Bureau of Labor Statistics is set to release October's employment data on Nov. 6. Economists project that employers added 55,000 jobs to payrolls in the month. That would be enough momentum to keep the national unemployment rate steady at 4.2%.

Most Fed officials are upbeat about labor conditions because unemployment trends remain historically low within the estimated bounds of full employment. The unemployment rate ticked up by just a tenth of a percentage point in September, and initial unemployment insurance claims have run at some of the lowest levels since the 1960s in recent weeks.

The Indeed Job Postings Index rose 0.3% in October, and the latest business surveys point to a stronger gain in payrolls over the past month. But new postings as defined by Indeed didn't improve in October.

ADP's measure of weekly private payrolls points to a monthly gain of around 65,000 jobs in October, down from September's reported advance of 90,000. The next ADP National Employment Report will be released Nov. 4.

LinkedIn reports that hiring in September remained 3.4% below its level of a year ago.

The data collectively point to a tight labor market, which stems largely from a lower supply of available workers. Restrictive immigration policies, deportations, and an aging workforce have shrunk the labor supply in the past few years, reducing hiring, which has kept the market in balance.

Although layoffs are relatively low, job prospects are challenging for the unemployed, writes Matthew Martin, senior U.S. economist at Oxford Economics. As of September, 27.1% of unemployed people had been jobless for more than 27 weeks, up from 24.7% in January.

The relative health of the labor market varies substantially by sector and even by region. Some sectors that once delivered reliable gains, such as healthcare and social assistance, are showing signs of slowing, while others aren't picking up the slack. Healthcare and social assistance, which includes support aides and social-work roles, have averaged 41,000 monthly job gains this year, down from an average monthly pace of 57,000 in 2025 and 74,000 in 2024.

Construction and manufacturing have reversed the hiring declines they saw over the past two years, both netting positive results since June. Still, the average monthly gain was only 18,000 year to date through September. The data-center buildout could lead to more gains in coming months, unless higher borrowing costs slow activity.

Policymakers may find themselves playing a tricky economic version of the classic game Operation. Can they remove the "ailment" of inflation without tripping the buzzer and further weakening the labor market? We'll find out in coming months if the Fed raises interest rates further.

Write to Megan Leonhardt at megan.leonhardt@barrons.com

data.title: South American Weather Comes Into Focus — Market Talk
data.description: A V-shaped rebound in grains is unlikely unless China comes to the U.S. market for grain in bulk, AgResource says in a note. Still, it's difficult to be bearish corn under $4.50 a bushel, wheat under $6 and soybeans under $12.30 unless favorable Brazilian weather is confirmed in November-December, the firm says. Brazilian forecasts will be in focus starting next week, and while there are no problems with Argentine soil moisture or pace of corn and soy planting, there is a significant risk of a lingering El Niño negatively affecting rainfall in key soybean producing regions of Brazil, AgResource adds. data.title: Cochilco cuts Chilean copper forecast for 2026, 2027
data.description:
Chile's copper commission Cochilco on Friday sharply lowered its forecast for Chilean copper production this year and forecast a milder-than-expected recovery for 2027.

The entity expects 2026 output to fall 8.4% versus a prior estimate of a 2.6% decline, before recovering next year with a 3% rise, slimmer than previously anticipated.

  • Cochilco estimates that Chilean copper production in 2026 will fall 8.4% to 4.94 million metric tons, versus an August estimate of 5.27 million tons

  • It noted that BHP's Escondida and Spence, along with state-run Codelco mines, account for more than 77% of Chile's net decline

  • Between January and September, Chile produced 3.63 million tons, down 8.5% from the same period in 2025

  • The country needs to produce close to 434,000 tons per month in the fourth quarter to reach the full-year estimate, Cochilco said

  • That amount would be 7.6% above average of what was produced this year through September

  • In 2027, Cochilco expects production to recover 3% to 5.08 million tons, versus the August estimate of 5.55 million tons

  • Lower ore grades, maintenance and disruptions have affected copper processing and recovery, Cochilco noted

  • Cochilco also raised its forecast for average copper prices to $6.18 per pound in 2026 and $5.95 per pound in 2027, citing constrained mine supply and a refined copper market with little room to absorb production disruptions

data.title: Valkea Approves Advance Notice Policy and Grants Stock Options
data.description:
Vancouver, British Columbia--(Newsfile Corp. - October 30, 2026) - Valkea Resources Corp. (TSXV: OZ) (OTCQB: OZBKF) (FSE: 4A7) (the "Company" or "Valkea") announces that the board of directors of the Company has adopted an advance notice policy (the "Advance Notice Policy").

The purpose of the Advance Notice Policy is to establish a process that provides shareholders, directors and management of the Company with direction on the nomination of directors. This Advance Notice Policy is the framework by which the Company seeks to fix a deadline by which holders of record of common shares of the Company must submit director nominations to the Company prior to any annual or special meeting of shareholders and sets forth the information that a shareholder must include in the notice to the Company for the notice to be in proper written form.

For all subsequent meetings of shareholders of the Company, the notice of a shareholder nominating a director (the "Nominating Shareholder") to the Corporate Secretary of the Company must be made:

  • in the case of an annual meeting of shareholders, not less than 30 days prior to the date of the annual meeting of shareholders; provided, however, that in the event that the annual meeting of shareholders is to be held on a date that is less than 50 days after the date (the "Notice Date") on which the first public announcement of the date of the annual meeting was made, notice by the Nominating Shareholder may be made not later than the close of business on the tenth (10th) day following the Notice Date in respect of such meeting; or
  • in the case of a special meeting (which is not also an annual meeting) of shareholders called for the purpose of electing directors (whether or not called for other purposes), not later than the close of business on the fifteenth (15th) day following the day on which the first public announcement of the date of the special meeting of shareholders was made.

The Advance Notice Policy is effective immediately. At the next annual meeting of shareholders, the Company is seeking shareholder approval and ratification of the Advance Notice Policy. In the event that shareholders determine not to ratify the Advance Notice Policy by ordinary resolution, the Advance Notice Policy shall terminate and be void and of no further force and effect following the termination of the meeting.

The full text of the Advance Notice Policy is available via SEDAR+ at www.sedarplus.ca or upon request by contacting Ota Hally, the Chief Financial Officer of the Company by e-mail at ohally@valkearesources.com. Further details on the Meeting and the Advance Notice Policy will be contained in a management information circular to be mailed to shareholders of the Company in connection with the next annual meeting of shareholders (the "Management Information Circular"). The Management Information Circular will also be available on SEDAR+.

Stock Option Grant

The Company also announces that it has granted an aggregate of 200,000 incentive stock options (the "Options") to an employee of the Company, to purchase up to 200,000 common shares ("Option Shares") in the capital of Valkea. The Options are exercisable at a price of $0.27 per share for a period of five (5) years from the date of grant, subject to vesting provisions. The Options will vest over two years, one third at grant, and one-third vesting every twelve months thereafter, in accordance with the Company's approved omnibus plan.

The Company believes that the issuance of these Options will further align the interests of its team with those of shareholders and will serve as an incentive for continued performance and commitment to the Company's growth.

About Valkea

Valkea Resources is a geoscience-led exploration company focused on making new gold and base metals discoveries in Northern Finlandʼs prospective Central Lapland Greenstone Belt. Its 350 km2 land package includes six principal project areas that span highly prospective regional geological structures. The Company's leadership and technical team include key contributors to the multimillion-ounce Ikkari gold discovery made in 2020. Work is underway to make a new discovery using the same systematic and disciplined approach to identifying targets with the best potential for meaningful size and the possibility of becoming mines of the future.

data.title: Tesla Stocks Move Lower With Cybercab Certification Response Due Today
data.description:
Tesla , the electric-vehicle and autonomous-driving company, faces a paperwork test for its Cybercab ambitions. Shares moved lower 0.79% to $400.12 at 12:30 p.m. ET on October 30 as a federal safety-certification response deadline arrived. At The Charger's report puts the focus on the documentation behind Tesla's certificationa hurdle that could matter as investors weigh its autonomous-driving plans.

The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration's September 29 memorandum records Tesla's request for an eight-week extension to November 20. The agency granted 30 days instead, setting October 30 as the response deadline. The audit examines the basis for Tesla's certification under federal vehicle-safety standards. Reaching that date does not mean the review is finished, nor does it guarantee that Tesla's answers will immediately become public.

The valuation leaves plenty riding on execution. GuruFocus shows a $1.58 trillion market capitalization and a price-to-earnings ratio of 440.17, suggesting investors are paying heavily for future earnings potential. Its GF Score of 87 out of 100, with growth the strongest chart component, sits alongside three severe warning signs whose details are not shown. That mix raises the stakes for concrete progress: a documented response or subsequent agency action could help investors judge how certification requirements may shape Cybercab deployment.

data.title: ADP 1Q 2027: Revenue $5.49B, EPS $2.83— 10-Q Summary
data.description:
Automatic Data Processing reported first-quarter fiscal 2027 revenue of $5.49 billion, up 6% from a year earlier. Net income rose 11% to $1.13 billion, while diluted earnings per share increased 14% to $2.83.

Financial Highlights

  • Revenue was $5.49B, compared with $5.18B in the prior-year quarter; YoY change 6%.
  • Net income was $1.13B, compared with $1.01B in the prior-year quarter; YoY change 11%.
  • Diluted EPS was $2.83, compared with $2.49 in the prior-year quarter; YoY change 14%.

Business Highlights

  • Organic constant-currency revenue growth was 6%, supported by new business, client retention, pricing and client-fund interest.
  • Employer Services revenue increased 6%. PEO Services revenue grew 7%, including 4% growth excluding zero-margin benefits pass-throughs.
  • ADP Assist reached more than 100,000 additional clients during the quarter, as ADP expanded AI agents across HR and talent workflows.
  • ADP Lyric HCM became available to companies headquartered in the U.K., France, Germany and the Netherlands.
  • U.S. pays per control grew 2%, and PEO average worksite employees increased 2% year over year.

Original SEC Filing: AUTOMATIC DATA PROCESSING INC [ ADP ] - 10-Q - Oct. 30, 2026

data.title: Stock Market Today: Deepening Tech Selloff Pushes Nasdaq Toward Its Worst Month in Over a Year — WSJ
data.description:
By Ed Ballard

The tech selloff is intensifying after results from Amazon and Intel compounded worries around the artificial intelligence trade.

The Nasdaq composite slumped more than 3%, while the S&P 500 lost 2.2% and the Dow industrials retreated more than 1%, or 630 points. For the tech-heavy Nasdaq, the selloff of the past two days has set the index up for its worst month since March 2025 and put it about 8.5% below its record high.

Shares of Amazon dropped about 2%; its earnings were in line with the company's forecasts-and showed booming cloud-computing growth-but left the market wanting more. Intel shares, meanwhile, are having their worst day ever, down 30% after the memory-chip crunch and other hiccups weighed on PC sales.

The AI worry comes with a side order of crypto angst in the wake of a massive cyberattack on Binance. Bitcoin and other cryptocurrencies are trading lower after hackers made off with an estimated $6.3 billion from an attack on the crypto exchange. Binance suspended transactions and said users will be made whole.

Meanwhile, oil is up after more strikes in the Middle East and Russia. Brent crude climbed to about $113 after a tanker transiting the Strait of Hormuz came under attack, according to U.K. Maritime Trade Operations. Ukraine struck an oil refinery in Russia, ending a pause that the Trump administration had pushed for.

This item is part of a Wall Street Journal live coverage event. The full stream can be found by searching P/WSJL (WSJ Live Coverage).

data.title: Basis bids steady as planting progresses
data.description:

  • Market players continued to monitor activity in the Black Sea grain export region after Russia allowed grain export vessels to leave the Sea of Azov for the first time since July 10, improving global supply prospects.

data.title: US SEC's top cop says agency is monitoring AI corporate disclosures
data.description:
By Chris Prentice

The US Securities and Exchange Commission is examining artificial intelligence companies' corporate disclosures as investor worries mount over a potential AI bubble that may have been fueled by circular deals, the agency's enforcement director told Reuters on Friday.

Big Tech stocks sold off this week as companies disclosed they are burning through cash to fuel their AI expansion at a time when interest rates are rising, raising questions about the sustainability of AI spending.

David Woodcock, who became SEC enforcement director in May, said the agency does not want to stand in the way of tech innovation, but that it is the agency's job to ensure issuers are giving investors the full picture on potential risks.

"Our principal concern is that people are making accurate disclosures about material information so that investors know what they're getting into," Woodcock said in an interview. "Enforcement is a very necessary piece of making sure people are doing that."

Where such disclosure does not happen, "then enforcement will be present," he said.

Woodcock also said that AI and superintelligence have made scams much easier and cheaper to manufacture at scale, raising risks for more and more people. Brokers and other firms need to have processes in place to protect retail investors and "take thoughtful action," he said.

PRIVATE MARKETS AND PREDICTION MARKETS

Woodcock said the SEC will continue to look at issues in private markets, adding that the enforcement team's asset management unit is very focused on conflicts of interest and valuations.

"When people don't make accurate disclosures, whether it's about valuations or whatever, then there is a role for enforcement," Woodcock said. "I think you'll see more activity in this space."

Reuters previously reported the SEC was probing a type of private equity fund as part of the agency's broader interest in the opaque markets.

Woodcock said the SEC also has a role in overseeing prediction markets, which allow people to bet on real-world events, including sports, government policy announcements and elections.

The markets, led by Polymarket and Kalshi, have surged in popularity over the past two years and have been pushing into US stocks. Such equity-linked prediction markets would traditionally fall under SEC jurisdiction.

Woodcock said the agency's enforcement staff are working with policy officials as well as the Commodity Futures Trading Commission, which broadly oversees swap markets, to monitor and regulate the booming new markets.

When asked about the possibility of bringing cases against firms that do not register with the agency, Woodcock said the agency does not want to regulate the new industry through enforcement actions.

"We want to be involved where it makes sense, but not in a way that crushes innovation," he said.

data.title: Govt names 1993-batch IAS officer Poundrik as heavy industries secretary
data.description:
NEW DELHI, Oct. 30 -- The appointments committee of the cabinet on Friday named 1993-batch Indian Administrative Service (IAS) officer Sandeep Poundrik as secretary of the ministry of heavy industries, according to an official order.

Poundrik, an IAS officer of the Bihar cadre, has been given additional charge of the heavy industries ministry while continuing as secretary of the steel ministry.

Union minister HD Kumaraswamy holds both the steel and heavy industries portfolios, and Poundrik's new responsibility means he will now head both ministries at the secretary level.

Poundrik's appointment comes at a time when crucial tasks for the heavy industries ministry would be to ensure smooth continuation of key electric mobility schemes such as the Rs.25,938-crore production-linked incentive scheme for automobiles and auto parts (PLI Auto) and the Rs.11,900-crore PM E-Drive scheme, while also ensuring that crucial advanced chemistry cell projects under the Rs.18,100-crore PLI scheme for advanced chemistry cells (PLI ACC) scheme takes off successfully.

The ministry also oversees operations at state-run Bharat Heavy Electricals Ltd (Bhel), an integral engineering and infrastructure sector public enterprise, which makes power generation equipment, transportation and railway equipment, defence and aerospace sector manufacturing, and clean energy products.

The ministry is also responsible for running the Rs.1,207 crore Scheme for Enhancement of Competitiveness in the Indian Capital Goods Sector - Phase II, under which the government runs industry accelerators and skilling programmes to reduce gaps in research and development in the capital goods sector.

In November 2025, the heavy industries ministry also launched a Rs.7,280-crore incentive package to set up five rare earth magnet making plants in the country, in the wake of a global rare earth magnet shortage caused by Chinese export controls in retaliation to steep US tariffs.

Rare earth magnets are made from monazite deposits, of which India is the world's third largest source. These magnets are made after processing monazite --- China controls around 60% of the world's rare earth mining and 90% of the world's rare earth processing capacity --- and these magnets are used in crucial manufacturing sectors such as defence, electronics, renewable energy, and automobiles including cleaner electric vehicles.

The PLI Auto and PLI ACC schemes, along with the PM E-Drive and the rare earth magnet making scheme, are crucial for advancing India's progress towards meeting the country's target of becoming a net-zero carbon emitter by 2070.

The government has supported the rollout of 1.1 million electric vehicles - 811,357 electric two-wheelers, 2,168 e-rickshaws (L3 category), 288,508 electric three-wheelers (L5 category), and 155 electric trucks - under the PM E-Drive scheme. The government has also sanctioned 14,000 e-buses under the scheme, through tenders issued by Convergence Energy Services Ltd (CESL).

Under the PLI Auto scheme, the government has disbursed Rs.2,386.86 crore by the end of FY26, with the scheme set to disburse incentives for manufacturing zero-emission vehicles till FY29. Currently, eight vehicle makers and 10 component makers are eligible to claim incentives under this scheme.

The PLI ACC scheme, which targets setting up of 50 GWh cell making capacity in the country, has seen delays in capacity creation, with just 1 GWh of the 40 GWh awarded installed as of March 2026. The government subsequently revised Ola Electric's timeline, allowing it to access incentives for its 20 GWh capacity through 2031. Reliance Industries, another beneficiary, has been allocated 15 GWh of capacity.

The ministry did not extend the same benefits to Bengaluru-based Rajesh Exports, which was awarded 5 GWh of capacity in 2022, citing allegations of financial misrepresentation involving around Rs.15 trillion levelled against the company by market regulator Securities and Exchange Board of India in June this year.

Another 10 GWh capacity under the scheme, earmarked for grid-scale energy storage services, is yet to be awarded. A tender for the same was floated in July.
